overview: The Agricultural Act of 2026 is a broad "farm bill" that renews and changes most Department of Agriculture programs through fiscal year 2031 (which ends September 30, 2031). It covers farm support and disaster aid, dairy programs, crop insurance, conservation programs that pay farmers to protect soil, water and wetlands, farm loans, rural development, agricultural research, forestry and energy. Its nutrition section changes SNAP, the food assistance program once called food stamps, by making online grocery purchasing permanent, allowing hot rotisserie chicken to be bought with benefits, and pushing back by a year a planned shift of some benefit costs to states, while requiring states with payment error rates of 10 percent or more to pay 20 percent of benefit costs starting in 2031. Other sections address food aid abroad, including a plan to move the Food for Peace program to the Agriculture Department, livestock disease, fertilizer reporting, year-round sales of E15 gasoline (a higher-ethanol blend), and country-of-origin labeling for beef and some seafood. As of September 24, 2026, the Senate agriculture committee had reported it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say the bill gives farmers, ranchers and rural communities several years of predictable programs, updates disaster and crop insurance help, and makes practical SNAP improvements while tightening accountability for states with high error rates.
against: Critics say shifting more SNAP costs to states with high error rates could squeeze state budgets and lead to cuts for families, and that a bill this large bundles many unrelated policies, such as fuel rules, into one package.
